How to do itCable Lateral Raise

Top height

Right
SHOULDER HEIGHT
Wrong
ABOVE SHOULDER

Right: Arm parallel with the floor, elbow slightly bent.

Wrong: Arm raised above shoulder height.

Elbow lead

Right
ELBOW LEADS
Wrong
HANDLE PULLED UP

Right: Breathe out. Elbow leads, hand follows, out to the side.

Wrong: Handle pulled straight up.

Step away from the machine so the cable is tight.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Above shoulderThe arm rises above shoulder height.
  2. Beyond 90°The upper arm goes past level, beyond 90 degrees.
Raise2 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

One single handle in your outside hand, the one farther from the machine.

Common handling mistakes

  • Raising above shoulder height

    Fix: Stop when your arm is parallel with the floor.

  • Swinging with momentum

    Fix: Go lighter and lift without swinging. Breathe in, lower with control.

  • Shrugging the shoulder

    Fix: Keep your shoulder down as the arm rises.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the side of your shoulder.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are shrugging the shoulder as the arm rises.

    FixKeep your shoulder down as the arm rises.

  • Usually meansYou are raising the arm above shoulder height.

    FixStop when your arm is parallel with the floor.

  • FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the pulley at its lowest point with a single handle.

  2. 2

    Stand upright, side-on to the machine. Handle in your outside hand.

  3. 3

    Step away until the cable is tight.

  4. 4

    Let the arm hang down, elbow slightly bent. Brace your torso.

  5. 5

    Pick a lighter weight than you think.

Risks and when to stop

  • Raises above shoulder height are linked with signs of shoulder pinching.
  • Raising straight out to the side hurts? Raise a little forward.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itDumbbell Front Raise

Arm height

Right
SHOULDER HEIGHT
Wrong
ABOVE SHOULDERS

Right: Arms level with the shoulders, parallel with the floor.

Wrong: Dumbbells raised above shoulder height.

Body still

Right
HIPS STILL
Wrong
HIPS FORWARD

Right: Body tall and still as the dumbbells rise.

Wrong: Hips pushed forward to swing the weights up.

Pull your shoulders down and back and hold them there.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Swinging upThe dumbbells swing up with body momentum.
  2. Hips forwardThe hips push forward to swing the weights up.
Raise1 s
Hold1 s
Lower3 s
Look closer

Grip

Closed grip, palms down, thumbs around the handles, dumbbells shoulder-width apart. Near the top, turn the inside edge slightly up.

Keep your wrists straight, not bent up or down.

Common handling mistakes

  • Swinging the weights up

    Fix: Use lighter dumbbells. Keep your hips still.

  • Arching the back

    Fix: Brace and keep your torso upright.

  • Raising above shoulder height

    Fix: Stop when your arms are level with your shoulders.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your shoulders and your upper chest.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansSwinging the weights adds stress here.

    FixUse lighter dumbbells and lift without swinging.

  • FixStop. Go much lighter, or raise slightly out to the sides.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Stand with feet slightly wider than hips, or in a split stance.

  2. 2

    Dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing them. Elbows slightly bent.

  3. 3

    Brace your torso and pull your shoulders down and back.

  4. 4

    Pick a lighter weight than you think.

  5. 5

    Breathe out, raise slowly. Breathe in, lower slowly, not onto your thighs.

Risks and when to stop

  • Shoulder: swinging the weights adds extra stress to the shoulder joints.
  • Shoulder: a slight outward turn near shoulder height may reduce shoulder pinching.
  • It is easy to pick a weight that is too heavy.

Shoulder pain

How to do itFace Pull

Elbow height

Right
ELBOWS HIGH
Wrong
ELBOWS DROP

Right: Elbows high and wide, rope to the face.

Wrong: Elbows below shoulder height.

Rope height

Right
EYE LEVEL
Wrong
TO THE CHIN

Right: Rope pulled toward the face at eye level.

Wrong: Rope pulled low, to the chin.

Keep the elbows high and wide for the whole rep.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows dropThe elbows drop below shoulder height during the pull.
  2. Pulled to chinThe rope is pulled too low, to the chin, not the face.
Pull2 s
Hold1 s
Return3 s
Look closer

Grip

Hands on the ends of the rope, palms facing each other. Pull the ends apart and squeeze your shoulder blades.

Common handling mistakes

  • Dropping the elbows

    Fix: Keep your elbows high.

  • Pulling too low

    Fix: Pull toward your face, not your chest or chin.

  • Momentum from the torso

    Fix: Start light and keep your whole body still.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the backs of your shoulders and between your shoulder blades.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe elbows are dropping.

    FixKeep your elbows high.

  • FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Attach a rope to the cable at about head height.

  2. 2

    Hands on the ends of the rope, palms facing each other.

  3. 3

    Step back until your arms are straight, with tension.

  4. 4

    Stand up straight, feet hip-width apart.

  5. 5

    Lift your chest, shoulders back. Neutral spine, no arching.

Risks and when to stop

  • Dropped elbows can pinch the shoulder.
  • Shoulder pain means stop.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

How to do itIncline Push-Up

Shoulders down

Right
SHOULDERS DOWN
Wrong
SHOULDERS SHRUG

Right: Feet back, shoulders down away from the ears.

Wrong: Feet close to the bench, shoulders shrugged.

Hip line

Right
STRAIGHT LINE
Wrong
LOW BACK DROPS

Right: Head, hips and heels in one line.

Wrong: Low back dropped, chest still up.

Keep your head, hips and heels in one line.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Feet too closeYour feet are too close to the bench.
  2. Shoulders shrugYour shoulder blades stay raised toward your ears.
Press3 s
Lower3 s
Look closer

Grip

Both hands on top of the bench, shoulder-width or a little wider.

Common handling mistakes

  • Feet too close, shoulders shrugged

    Fix: Walk your feet back so your shoulders sit down.

  • Elbows flaring too wide

    Fix: Keep your elbows about 45 degrees from your body.

  • Low back dropping

    Fix: Keep your hips in line with your shoulders.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your chest, front shoulders and triceps. Breathe in going down, out going up.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansShrugged shoulders or wide elbows load the shoulder more.

    FixWalk your feet back and keep your elbows at 45 degrees.

  • FixEnd the set when your low back starts to drop.

  • Usually meansLooking up can strain your neck.

    FixKeep your gaze straight ahead.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Use a sturdy bench or box that holds your weight.

  2. 2

    Hands on top, shoulder-width or a little wider.

  3. 3

    Walk your feet back until your body slopes at 45 degrees.

  4. 4

    Brace, squeeze glutes and thighs. Body in one line, head to heels.

  5. 5

    Shoulders back and down, away from your ears.

Risks and when to stop

  • Feet too close shrugs the shoulders and may raise shoulder injury risk.
  • Elbows flared wide add stress to the shoulder.

How to do itPike Push-Up

Head path

Right
FORWARD AND DOWN
Wrong
HEAD STRAIGHT DOWN

Right: Head moves forward and down, neck neutral.

Wrong: Only the head moves toward the floor.

Hips high

Right
HIPS HIGH
Wrong
HIPS SAG

Right: Legs straight, hips high in an upside-down V.

Wrong: Hips sagging toward the floor.

Keep your legs straight and your hips up in an upside-down V.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Head straight downOnly your head drops toward the floor, straight down.
Lower 
Press 
Look closer

Grip

Hands about shoulder-width. Spread your fingers for a stable base.

Common handling mistakes

  • Elbows flaring out

    Fix: Tuck your elbows in. Too hard? Go back to standard push-ups.

  • Moving only your head down

    Fix: Chin slightly tucked. Move your head forward and down.

  • Holding your breath

    Fix: Breathe in going down, out going up.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your shoulders and the back of your arms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansFlared elbows can hurt the shoulder over time.

    FixTuck your elbows in, or go back to standard push-ups.

  • Usually meansUpside down, holding your breath can make you dizzy.

    FixBreathe in going down, out going up.

  • Usually meansYour hands carry more of your weight here.

    FixUse push-up handles or a soft mat.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Start in a push-up position, hands about shoulder-width.

  2. 2

    Brace and pull your shoulders down and back.

  3. 3

    Keep your legs straight and lift your hips into a V.

  4. 4

    Walk your hands toward your feet to get more upside down.

  5. 5

    Spread your fingers for a stable base. Squeeze your abs.

Risks and when to stop

  • Elbows flaring out can lead to shoulder injury over time.
  • Upside down, holding your breath can make you dizzy or light-headed.
  • Moving only your head toward the floor raises injury risk.
